extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity (scientists, research administrators, journalists, and the general public following retractions)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical triggers that lead journals or publishers to investigate and retract biomedical research articles, as illustrated by cases of alleged image manipulation. Focus is on image-related misconduct, post-publication critiques, editorial investigation steps, and responses (or non-responses) by authors and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image duplication (identical or similar images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles contained images and figures that appeared similar or identical to others in the same paper or published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The retraction notices cite image duplication across panels or across publications as a reason for retraction; such duplications are treated as substantive problems regardless of citation counts or publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images used to represent different experimental conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Image elements have been used to represent different experimental conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals noted specifically when the same image element was presented as evidence for distinct experimental conditions, which is grounds for retraction because it misrepresents the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unresolved image concerns that undermine integrity and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Unresolved image concerns that call into question the integrity and reliability of the reported results and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When concerns about images cannot be satisfactorily resolved, editors may determine that the reliability of findings is compromised and retract the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party/reader-raised concerns triggering investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations often begin after ‘multiple readers’ or third parties bring concerns to editors (e.g., via PubPeer or direct contact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication critiques and reader reports are a common trigger for publisher investigations; journals may act on numerous secondary concerns received from third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence from post-publication peer review platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Public commentary on platforms like PubPeer noting apparent image similarities or duplications in papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public, post-publication commentary can document suspected problems and prompt formal editorial review; such documented observations are treated as substantive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsiveness to editorial communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether authors respond to editorial communications related to concerns and to retraction decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors report author engagement (e.g., responding to early communications) or lack thereof; non-response to decisions or to inquiries can factor in the process and public reporting of retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial assessment and triage (initial assessment of other articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers perform an ‘initial assessment’ of other articles by the same authors to determine if similar concerns appear elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may conduct a broader review of an author’s body of work; if no similar concerns are identified, further action may be limited to the specific problematic papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional editorial remedy: retraction versus editorial note
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions between full retraction and issuing an editorial note based on the nature and severity of the concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all problematic findings lead to retraction; some issues (e.g., problems deemed less severe or resolvable) may be addressed with an editorial note rather than removal of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should specify reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction statements list the specific problems (for example, image duplication or use of images to represent different conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public retraction notices serve to explain why the record is being corrected; clear specification of the problematic elements is part of transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional response and history of misconduct matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions’ prior involvement in misconduct cases and their responses (or lack of response) to inquiries are relevant context for retractions and investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes institutional histories (e.g., prior sanctions, settlements, bans) and whether the university responds to inquiries; institutional accountability and communication can be scrutinized alongside journal actions.
